preamble: In Sotho-Tswana, root-initial /r/ hardens to the aspirated stop [tʰ] in post-nasal contexts, part of a broader post-nasal fortition that also turns /l/ into [t], /f/ into [pʰ] and /s/ into [tsʰ]. In Setswana the change is triggered by the reflexive prefix, the 1st person singular object marker and the class 9 noun prefix, all of which historically contained a homorganic nasal; the nasal itself is often lost while its effect remains. Acoustic VOT values of the derived [tʰ] match underlying /tʰ/, so the shift is categorical. Northern Sotho shows the same pattern: rata 'love' gives reflexive ithata 'love oneself' and nthata 'love me' with the 1st person singular object prefix.

examples.note: The reflexive prefix /i(N)-/ surfaces as [i-] but still triggers hardening of root-initial /r/ to [tʰ].
The reflexive prefix i- changes root-initial r to aspirated th; Prinsloo lists this among reflexives with sound change but no semantic shift.
The 1st person singular object prefix N- triggers the same hardening, alongside l > t (lebala > itebala/ntebala) and f > ph (fahla > iphahla/mphahla).

sources: Bennett, W. G., Diemer, M., Kerford, J., Probert, T., & Wesi, T. (2016). Setswana (South African). Journal of the International Phonetic Association 46(2), 235-246. https://doi.org/10.1017/S0025100316000050
